title: Invalid mouse method config is treated as an empty allowlist instead of being ignored
reasoning: When tool_options.mouse_control.enabled_coordinate_methods is present but not an array, the parser logs that it is ignoring the invalid value, but still assigns mouse_methods to an empty frozenset. Downstream, an empty frozenset means mouse_control has no allowed coordinate methods, which disables mouse_control and prevents OCR/vision initialization. That contradicts the warning's stated behavior and makes a malformed dev config disable local desktop capability rather than falling back to the default of all coordinate methods. The existing startup-service test covers an explicit valid manual-only list, not the malformed-config path.
recommendation: Only assign mouse_methods when enabled_coordinate_methods is a valid list/tuple/set, or leave it as None for malformed values so the default all-methods behavior is preserved. If fail-closed behavior is intentional, change the warning and add an explicit test documenting that invalid config disables all coordinate methods.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise valid coordinate-method lists and the resulting OCR/vision startup gating, but do not cover a malformed enabled_coordinate_methods value despite the parser having a specific invalid-value branch.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that loads a config with [tool_options.mouse_control] enabled_coordinate_methods = "manual" and asserts get_allowed_mouse_coordinate_methods() returns manual, ocr, and prediction, and should_initialize_ocr()/should_initialize_vision() remain true.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/tools/tool_selection.py _parse_selection plus one focused backend test in tests/backend/test_tool_policy.py or a dedicated tool_selection test.
